Consequently Spring Boot applications using Log4j still capture no MapMessage attributes and do not apply this common selector, contrary to this metadata and the PR description. Please wire the common selector into the Spring Log4j setup while preserving explicit standalone appender controls.

That adds per-entry predicate and atomic-read overhead to the logging hot path for users whose behavior should remain unchanged. Keep the mapper selector nullable while the default is unset, and update it when the two-argument installer supplies a selector (for example, via mutable selector state in the mapper).

threads.body: [General] Removing the prefix means this loop now passes raw `MapMessage` keys to `AttributeKey.stringKey`. Log4j accepts an empty-string map key, but OpenTelemetry rejects an empty attribute key, so one such entry makes the appender throw and drop the log; the old `log4j.map_message.` prefix kept this case valid. Skip empty keys before creating the attribute key.

threads.body: [Config] Converting an absent or empty common selector into an explicit `included=["*"]` selector makes it override `structuredAttributesIncluded` / `structuredAttributesExcluded` declared in `logback.xml`. For example, a Spring application with `<structuredAttributesExcluded>*</structuredAttributesExcluded>` and no corresponding Spring property will unexpectedly capture everything. Preserve an empty selector here so the appender can fall back to its XML selector and only use the capture-all default when both sources are empty.

[Testing] This test only calls the installer helper on a capturing setter and checks `IncludeExclude.matches`; it does not verify the changed Spring Boot initialization path or emitted logs. It would still pass if the listener failed to apply/restart the real appender or if the mapper ignored the selector. Add an end-to-end Spring Logback test that starts the application with the common property, emits a supported structured source, and asserts the exported attributes (including an exclusion).
